issues.title: Undefined convection traces under the stated coefficient class
issues.failure_explanation: The old construction accepts a divergence-free beta in L-infinity but evaluates jumps and ordinary L2 face integrals of u_h tensor beta. The paper's own jump definition requires broken H1 regularity, which L-infinity does not provide. Thus the DG form is not a well-defined executable construction for every admitted beta.
issues.overall_effect: The DG form and the general-coefficient proofs using its convection fluxes are only valid after adding trace regularity. The later polynomial-coefficient efficiency analysis is not affected by this root because its shared polynomial qualification supplies the needed traces.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Impose a standing trace-regularity hypothesis on the divergence-free convection field, for example β ∈ W^{1,∞}(Ω)^d, before defining the DG form, and make every general-coefficient result in the affected chain conditional on it. This makes the convection fluxes ordinary face functions and validates the face integrals, Green identities, consistency, coercivity, and reliability arguments without changing their conclusions or rates.
issues.why_classification: This is a contained assumption-level repair, but replacing the stated L-infinity class by a Lipschitz class excludes a genuine natural regime of bounded, possibly discontinuous convection fields. The regular-coefficient method and all affected guarantees remain recognizably the same, so the loss is limited rather than major; the issue is therefore moderate rather than minor or serious.

issues.title: Coercivity stated without the penalty threshold
issues.failure_explanation: The lower bound in the proof contains gamma minus positive terms depending on the Young parameters and the convection field. It becomes coercive only after gamma is chosen above those terms. Thus the proof establishes conditional, not unconditional, coercivity.
issues.overall_effect: The stability, source-problem, and spectral conclusions relying on discrete coercivity are valid only in the sufficiently-large-penalty regime already selected in the proof.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State in Lemma 2.1 that coercivity holds only for γ at or above a sufficiently large threshold depending on the fixed coefficients, polynomial degree, and mesh-regularity constants, and adopt that threshold as a standing hypothesis for every listed stability, source, spectral, and reliability result.
issues.why_classification: The proof itself explicitly selects a sufficiently large γ and already contains the terms determining the threshold. Adding this standard interior-penalty qualification is short and routine and preserves the method, conclusions, and rates in the intended stable-penalty regime. It is a genuine missing premise, so it is not merely a typo.

issues.title: Missing conjugation in the discrete adjoint definition
issues.failure_explanation: The operator construction in s2.57 omits the conjugation around B_h(v,S_h* f). Its two left-hand terms then have incompatible dependence on the complex test function, so the object defined there is not the adjoint source operator used to claim s2.61.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed discrete-adjoint operator definition and its claimed adjoint identity are inconsistent, leaving the adjoint-operator part of the spectral analysis unjustified as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the first equation in s2.57 by A_h(v,T_h* f) + overline(B_h(v,S_h* f)) = (v,f). The zero constraint may remain conjugated because conjugating an equation equal to zero is equivalent. With this correction, the operator repeats the adjoint source problem in s2.52 and the identity s2.61 follows.
issues.why_classification: The preceding adjoint source equation s2.52 and the complex linearity in the test function uniquely force the missing conjugation. The literal formula mixes linear and conjugate-linear dependence, while the one-symbol correction restores the already-defined construction without changing any argument or guarantee; this is transcriptional.

issues.title: Missing adjoint source regularity

failure_location.quote: By the same argument as for (\ref{s2.75}), we obtain (\ref{s2.76}).

issues.failure_explanation: The old paper assumes H1+r by Hr regularity only for the primal source solution. The proof of s2.75 may use that primal dual solution, but the analogous proof of s2.76 requires T* f and S* f to have the same regularity, which is not assumed. Consequently operator convergence and the later adjoint-eigenfunction interpolation quantities are not established under the old hypotheses.
issues.overall_effect: The primal L2 source estimate, the resulting operator-norm and spectral chain, and the eigenvalue-reliability result are conditional on an unstated adjoint regularity property.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert the uniform adjoint shift estimate before Theorem 2.5. If (u^{f*},p^{f*}) solves the adjoint source problem, skew-adjointness of the divergence-free convection term rewrites it as the primal Oseen source problem with right-hand side f + 2(β·∇)u^{f*}. The existing H1 stability and primal regularity estimate s2.25 then give ||u^{f*}||_{1+r} + ||p^{f*}||_r ≤ C||f||_0. Use this estimate in the proof of s2.76 and throughout the listed operator, spectral, and reliability chain.
issues.why_classification: The missing dependency requires a genuine argument, so it is not a typo. However, the companion regularity estimate follows by a short lower-order perturbation argument from stability and the already-assumed primal shift theorem, preserving the original hypotheses, rates, method, and all affected conclusions. No new proof architecture is needed.

issues.title: Unaligned eigenvectors in a multiple semisimple eigenspace
issues.failure_explanation: The old hypotheses permit a semisimple eigenspace of dimension greater than one. One may then choose a normalized continuous eigenvector different from the direction approached by u_h; the left side of s2.89 can remain bounded away from zero while the operator approximation term tends to zero. Spectral approximation controls the eigenspace gap, not arbitrarily indexed basis vectors.
issues.overall_effect: The individual eigenfunction estimates, and cluster statements that treat indexed eigenvectors as aligned, require a compatible choice of continuous eigenvectors; the subspace and averaged-eigenvalue conclusions are not defeated by this root.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: For each discrete eigenvector in a multiple semisimple cluster, choose the continuous eigenvector compatibly by the Riesz projection, for example u = E u_h/||E u_h||_0, with p = λSu, and make the analogous adjoint choice. Prove for small h that ||u_h-u||_0 is controlled by ||(T-T_h)u||_0, then state the individual and cluster estimates only for these aligned choices, or equivalently in basis-invariant subspace form.
issues.why_classification: Arbitrary bases in a multiple eigenspace cannot satisfy the claimed pairwise estimates. Retaining the multiple-eigenvalue regime and the same rates requires a spectral-projection construction and a contained but nontrivial alignment lemma, followed by corresponding changes to the dependent cluster statements. This avoids both global reconstruction and mathematical loss but exceeds a routine local repair.

issues.title: Reversed arguments in the adjoint residual formula
issues.failure_explanation: The old adjoint bound claims control by tilde A_h(u*-u_h*,v), whereas applying the second inf-sup relation gives tilde A_h(v,u*-u_h*). Convection makes the form nonsymmetric, so these expressions cannot be interchanged. The proof's statement that the primal argument applies similarly therefore supports the revised orientation, not the old one.
issues.overall_effect: The adjoint half of Theorem 3.1 and the adjoint reliability and eigenvalue-reliability results depending on it are not established with the old ordering.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: In s3.9 replace the term tilde A_h(u*−u_h*,v) by tilde A_h(v,u*−u_h*), leaving the adjoint pressure terms in their stated positions. Then apply the second inf-sup relation in s2.7; the resulting orientation agrees with the adjoint residual formula used in s3.13 and restores the downstream reliability arguments.
issues.why_classification: The second inf-sup relation and the old adjoint residual calculation uniquely force the argument order. Because the convection form is nonsymmetric, the old order is malformed for the stated adjoint argument, but swapping the two arguments is a transcriptional correction that changes no intended theorem, rate, or proof mechanism.

issues.title: Primal variables used in the adjoint reliability step
issues.failure_explanation: For the adjoint estimate in th3-1, the q-dependent residual is B'_h(u_h*,q). Old s3.13 instead supplies a bound for B'_h(u_h,q) and div u_h. Those are independent primal quantities, so the 'similarly' step in th3-4 invokes a bound that does not establish its required adjoint residual.
issues.overall_effect: The adjoint reliability estimate in th3-4, and hence the eigenvalue and cluster reliability conclusions using it, are unsupported until the residual variables are corrected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: In the adjoint residual estimate s3.13, replace u_h by u_h* in B'_h(u_h,q) and replace every accompanying ||div u_h|| term by ||div u_h*||. Invoke this corrected starred estimate in the adjoint part of Theorem 3.4 and its listed dependents.
issues.why_classification: Every surrounding quantity in s3.13 is adjoint, and s3.9 uniquely requires the residual of u_h*. The unstarred variables are copied primal notation rather than a mathematical choice; restoring the stars leaves the argument and all guarantees unchanged.

issues.title: Invalid global residual aggregation in the reliability proof
issues.failure_explanation: From the old s3.12 one has sums of local residual magnitudes and elementwise divergence norms. Bounding those linear sums by the global l2 estimator introduces a mesh-dependent factor. Therefore the one-line substitution in th3-4 does not prove its mesh-independent reliability constant, even though the earlier calculation s3.15 indicates how to obtain a valid square-summed estimate.
issues.overall_effect: The primal and adjoint reliability theorem, and the eigenvalue and cluster reliability results using it, lack a mesh-independent proof until the local residuals are aggregated in l2.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the linear residual sums in s3.12 and its adjoint analogue by square-summed bounds: use the square root of Στ(η_Rτ²+η_Fτ²+η_Jτ²) times ||∇v||_0 and the square root of Στ||div u_h||²_{0,τ} times ||q||_0, with starred quantities for the adjoint estimate. Derive these bounds by Cauchy–Schwarz over elements and faces, finite overlap, and interpolation stability, then combine them with the enriching estimate to obtain Theorem 3.4 and its dependents with mesh-independent constants.
issues.why_classification: The old one-line substitution makes a genuine invalid aggregation and therefore is not a typo. Nevertheless, s3.15 already contains the required square-summed structure, and completing the proof only needs routine Cauchy–Schwarz and finite-overlap bookkeeping. The repair is local and preserves the estimators, conclusions, and rates without a new lemma or proof architecture.
